newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet shares fall on paper report.
newsitem.headline: Eramet shares fall on paper report.

text.p: Shares in nickel producer Eramet fell on Friday as investors worried about the possible ouster of chairman Yves Rambaud, dealers said.
At 0942 GMT Eramet was off 4.76 percent to 300 francs.
Eramet has gained 15 percent since the start of the year, helped by a strong dollar and rising nickel prices.

French daily Les Echos said earlier that although government had dropped plans to change the company's legal status, it might still try to replace Rambaud at the next shareholders meeting in June. "The possible ouster of Rambaud scares a market that likes this chairman," one dealer said.
Investors initially feared the change in legal status would herald the ouster of Rambaud, who opposed plans to curb Eramet's expansion in New Caledonia.
A compromise was eventually reached but Eramet is now involved in a dispute with the state over the cost of electricity supplies in New Caledonia, Les Echos said.
Dealers also said Eramet, a speculative stock, was hit by worries about the uncertain outlook for the nickel market.
"It is settlement day and speculators are squaring positions," one dealer said.
